proposals.name: IntrinsicMotivationSystem
proposals.description: Generates self-driven goals for agents based on their personality traits and beliefs when basic biological needs are satisfied, preventing idle behavior and simulating free will.

specification.name: IntrinsicMotivationSystem
specification.description: Generates self-driven goals for agents based on their personality traits and beliefs when basic biological needs are satisfied, preventing idle behavior and simulating free will.
specification.logic: 1. Iterates through all agents possessing Mind, Personality, and Needs components. 2. Checks if critical biological needs (Hunger, Energy) are above a safety threshold (e.g., > 40%). 3. Verifies if the agent lacks an active Goal or has a 'Wait'/'Idle' goal. 4. If the agent is free, evaluates Personality traits (e.g., Openness, Extraversion) and current Beliefs to formulate a new objective. 5. Assigns a new Goal (e.g., 'Investigate Object' for high Openness, 'Socialize' for high Extraversion, 'Organize' for high Conscientiousness). 6. Generates a corresponding Thought (e.g., 'I feel like doing something useful') to rationalize the new action.

proposals.rationale: Currently, all 12 agents have 0 active goals and neutral arousal. The simulation is in a state of stasis. This system would parse Personality, Needs, and Belief components to generate short-term and long-term goals, transforming the agents from passive observers into active participants.

specification.description: Defines an entity as hidden from normal view, requiring specific conditions or stats to be detected and revealed.

fields.name: detectionDifficulty
fields.description: The perception or investigation threshold required to spot this secret.

fields.name: isRevealed
fields.description: Whether the secret has been discovered and is currently visible to observers.

fields.name: revealMessage
fields.description: The narrative text displayed when the secret is successfully discovered.

proposals.rationale: To deepen SocialDynamics and RelationshipEvolution, agents need unique, non-public information. A Secret component provides a currency for social exchange, a catalyst for NarrativeEvents (revelations, blackmail, bonding), and a way to differentiate agent 'Mind' states beyond basic stats.

proposals.name: OccupationalGoalSystem
proposals.description: Drives agents to perform professional duties and work tasks based on their personality, available tools, and current role, distinguishing between leisure and productivity.

specification.name: OccupationalGoalSystem
specification.description: Drives agents to perform professional duties and work tasks based on their personality, available tools, and current role, distinguishing between leisure and productivity.
specification.logic: 1. Select agents possessing a Mind and Personality who are not InCombat. 2. Check Needs; if Hunger or Energy is critical, abort to allow survival systems to take priority. 3. Review the current Goal; if the agent is idle or performing a low-priority wandering task, initiate work logic. 4. Analyze Inventory for specific tools (e.g., weapon implies Guard, hoe implies Farmer) and check Description for role keywords. 5. Based on findings, generate a new high-priority Goal (e.g., 'Patrol', 'Harvest', 'Craft'). 6. Insert a Thought into the Mind reflecting a desire to be productive (e.g., 'I should earn my keep today.').

proposals.rationale: All 12 agents currently have 0 goals, resulting in a narrative standstill. This system would derive procedural goals from an agent's Description and Name (e.g., Ada the Baker should seek ingredients; Mayor Aldric should visit the Town Square), providing the necessary momentum for the GentleGoalSystem to process.

proposals.name: TradeInteractionSystem
proposals.description: Orchestrates the exchange of goods between agents based on the mutual coincidence of wants, utility calculation, and personality-driven valuation.

specification.name: TradeInteractionSystem
specification.description: Orchestrates the exchange of goods between agents based on the mutual coincidence of wants, utility calculation, and personality-driven valuation.
specification.logic: 1. Identifies agents with an active 'Trade' or 'Acquire' Goal who are spatially adjacent to another agent. 2. Scans the target agent's Inventory for items that satisfy the initiator's critical Needs or align with their Personality traits (e.g., Greed). 3. Calculates a 'Subjective Value' for potential exchange items based on current Need levels and Item rarity. 4. Determines willingness to trade by comparing the Subjective Value of items offered versus items requested, modified by Personality (Generosity/Greed). 5. If the trade logic evaluates as positive for both parties (or valid coercion/charity exists), moves the Item(s) between the respective Inventory lists. 6. Updates Memory for both agents regarding the fairness of the transaction. 7. Marks the 'Trade' Goal as complete.

proposals.rationale: Currently, agents like Greta the Merchant and Bjorn the Blacksmith have no mechanism to exchange items. A trade system would allow agents to fulfill their 'Needs' component by bartering or purchasing goods from one another, turning the static Inventory into a dynamic flow of resources.

proposals.name: MarketValue
proposals.description: Determines the economic worth, currency standard, and trade eligibility of an entity.

specification.name: MarketValue
specification.description: Determines the economic worth, currency standard, and trade eligibility of an entity.

fields.name: basePrice
fields.description: The intrinsic monetary value of the entity before market modifiers.

fields.name: currency
fields.description: The denomination code for the value (e.g., 'GP', 'Credits', 'Souls').

fields.name: isTradable
fields.description: Whether this entity can be bought or sold in standard markets.

fields.name: volatility
fields.description: A factor (0.0-1.0) determining how susceptible this item is to supply and demand fluctuations.

proposals.rationale: Items currently lack a 'Value' or 'Price' attribute. Adding a MarketValue component to Items—which can be modified by the agent's Personality (e.g., greed) or the local supply—is essential for emergent negotiation behaviors and establishing a hierarchy of wealth within the village.
